current_summary: Welcome: brand mark, wordmark, one-line pitch, three tinted feature rows, 'Get started' (→ sign-up) and a secondary 'I already have an account' (→ sign-in). Sign-in: two-word heading, optional 'Sign in to join {household}' banner, Sign in with Apple, Google, email + password fields (username/password content types, return-key chaining), Sign in, 'Forgot password?', 'New here? Create an account'. Sign-up: heading + subtitle, Apple (SIGN_UP), Google, display name / email / password (8+), Create account; a refused sign-up that advises signing in shows a Sign in button. Cost today: Welcome→inside via Apple = 2 taps + Face ID; returning email user = 2 taps 0 keystrokes IF QuickType offers the pair (declared, needs the webcredentials build) else ~4 taps + ~32 keystrokes; new email user = 3 fields (~40 keystrokes, or ~25 + one tap for the suggested password) + 1 tap.

apps.name: Notion (mobile + web)
apps.what: One login screen for both new and returning people: Continue with Google / Apple / Microsoft, or an email field; email sends a temporary login code (and a magic link) instead of asking for a password; passkeys supported. Apple/Google work only when the email matches.

aspects.aspect: One door — no sign-in vs sign-up fork; the server decides from the email
aspects.why: Welcome's second button and the two mirrored screens exist only to route people; a single email-first screen removes one decision and one screen

aspects.aspect: Emailed code instead of a password
aspects.why: Nothing to forget, so the reset flow disappears for most people

apps.name: Craft
apps.what: Login screen lists email, Apple, Google, Microsoft, SSO. Email → a 6-digit verification code from the inbox; Continue with Apple asks whether to share the email; Hide My Email produces a relay address.

aspects.aspect: 6-digit code that iOS Security Code AutoFill can fill
aspects.why: Turns the second step into one tap on the QuickType bar rather than typing

apps.name: Slack
apps.what: Open app → Sign in → choose a method: password, or 'Sign in with Email' which emails a confirmation code (or a magic link); SSO where required.

aspects.aspect: Code sign-in doubles as the recovery path
aspects.why: A person who forgot their password still gets in; password reset becomes an account-settings chore rather than a front-door flow

apps.name: Things 3 / Things Cloud
apps.what: No account to start; the account is created from Settings → Things Cloud when sync is wanted: email + password → Continue → Terms checkbox → 4-digit emailed code → Continue.

aspects.aspect: Verification is a 4-digit code inside the app, not an email link that leaves it
aspects.why: The user never has to find their way back to the app; Ambry's reset link round-trips through Mail

apps.name: Duolingo
apps.what: Value first: start → language → goal → placement quiz → lesson result → then 'create a profile' (age, name, email, password) mid-flow; account creation is skippable and re-prompted later.

aspects.aspect: Defer everything that is not needed to proceed
aspects.why: Ambry requires an account (spec 37 retired anonymity) but does NOT need a display name at sign-up — Apple supplies it and Profile → Your name already exists as the editor

apps.name: Apple HIG — Sign in with Apple, Onboarding, Password AutoFill
apps.what: Button no smaller than other sign-in buttons and never below the fold; titles limited to Sign in / Sign up / Continue with Apple; welcome people immediately after Apple sign-in; postpone non-essential setup; QuickType offers the saved pair only for an associated domain with username/password content types.

aspects.aspect: 'Continue with Apple' as the one title on a merged door
aspects.why: The same button is valid for new and returning people, which is what a single screen needs

aspects.aspect: Postpone non-essential setup; welcome immediately
aspects.why: Argues for dropping the display-name field and for no interstitial after Apple sign-in

aspects.aspect: QuickType credential pair needs the association + content types
aspects.why: This is the 2-tap sign-in Ambry already declared; the design only holds once the webcredentials build ships

directions.name: One door
directions.pitch: Welcome's single CTA opens one 'Continue' screen; the email decides whether you are new or returning.
regions: Heading 'Continue to Ambry' (accessibilityRole=header)
InviteBanner when a stash exists
Sign in with Apple (Continue), then Google
Divider 'or use email'
Input email (username content type, clearButton, returnKey go)
Button 'Continue' (disabled until an address)
State 2, returning: password Input appears under the email (QuickType offers the pair) + 'Sign in' + 'Forgot password?' link
State 2, new: password Input with newPassword + passwordRules (iOS suggests) + 'Create account' + one line 'Free to start. You can add your name later.'
FailureNotice for refusals; unreachable → notice + retry; RATE_LIMITED shows the server's words

borrowed.aspect: Continue with Apple title, no scrolling

directions.cost: Apple: 1 tap + Face ID from Welcome (was 2). Returning email: 2 taps 0 keystrokes with QuickType (unchanged). New email: ~20 keystrokes + 1 tap suggested password + 2 taps (was ~40 + 1).
directions.tradeoff: Needs a 'does this address have a password account' step — either a Worker probe (an explicit enumeration oracle; spec 28 §Hardening accepts sign-up as one already, bounded by the 10/min credential bucket) or Better Auth's sign-in-then-sign-up laundering. Decision for Everett. Removes the second Welcome button (agency: fewer forks, same reach).

directions.name: Code, not password
directions.pitch: Email → 6-digit emailed code, auto-filled by iOS; passwords stay for accounts that have them.
regions: Heading
Apple, Google
Input email + 'Email me a code'
State 2: 'We sent a code to {email}' + one-time-code Input (textContentType oneTimeCode, numeric pad) + 'Continue' + 'Use password instead' + 'Resend' (60 s cool-down)
Neutral copy on every address (no enumeration)
FailureNotice; unreachable → retry

borrowed.aspect: Code sign-in as the recovery path

directions.cost: New or returning: ~20 keystrokes (email) + 1 tap + 1 QuickType tap + 1 tap; 0 passwords to invent or forget. Forgot-password disappears for code users.
directions.tradeoff: Contradicts docs/adr/auth.md O2 (magic-link deliberately omitted for attack surface) — a PR-description escalation, not a silent divergence. Adds a Worker route (Better Auth email-OTP plugin) and a Resend template; an inbox round-trip per sign-in for people without a saved pair; enumeration-neutral copy required.

directions.name: Two screens, two fields
directions.pitch: Keep the fork; drop the display-name field so sign-up is email + suggested password.
regions: Welcome unchanged (bordered secondary now exists via P1)
Sign-up: heading + subtitle, Apple, Google, email, password (newPassword) — no name field
Create account; refusal → Sign in button (as today)
Post-sign-up: Profile's 'Your name' row is empty until set; Members list falls back to the email local-part

borrowed.aspect: Ask only what is required up front

directions.cost: Sign-up: 2 fields (~20 keystrokes + 1 suggested-password tap + 1 tap) from 3 (~40 + 1). Sign-in unchanged.
directions.tradeoff: Smallest blast radius; keeps two mirrored screens (the duplication the brief dislikes). Needs a display-name fallback wherever a member is named (spec 17 already tolerates an empty name).

current_summary: Forgot: in-screen title, optional expired/unusable notice, explainer, email Input (emailAddress), 'Send reset link' (disabled until an address), 'Back to sign in'; a sent request replaces the form with a mail glyph, the neutral no-enumeration sentence, 'Back to sign in' and 'Use a different email'. Reset (arrives by Universal Link, token held unexamined): title, one new-password field (newPassword + passwordRules), 'Set new password', 'Cancel — back to sign in'; success routes to sign-in with 'Password updated…' because Better Auth issues no session. Cost today: ~20 keystrokes (the email is NOT carried over from sign-in) + 1 tap → Mail → tap link → 1 tap suggested password + 1 tap → sign-in screen → 2 more taps. Three screens plus an inbox round-trip.

apps.name: Slack
apps.what: Sign in with an emailed confirmation code instead of the password; the password reset itself lives in Account settings → Password → 'Reset your password by email' (8+ chars).

aspects.aspect: Recovery = sign in with a code; password change is a settings task
aspects.why: Most locked-out people just want in; changing the password can happen later, signed in

apps.name: Apple Account
apps.what: On a trusted iPhone: Settings → [name] → Sign-In & Security → Change Password, gated by the device passcode rather than the old password; borrowed device via the Support app; iforgot.apple.com on the web; account recovery last.

aspects.aspect: Possession of a signed-in device is the proof
aspects.why: Ambry has no 'Change password' inside the app at all — today the only route is signing out and using the forgot flow

apps.name: Instagram
apps.what: 'Forgot password?' / 'Get help logging in' → enter username, email or phone → choose email or SMS → a login link or code; the link signs you in, then you may reset. Help page covers the not-received case (spam, wrong address).

aspects.aspect: Channel choice and a link that logs you in directly
aspects.why: The reset link doing the sign-in removes the re-sign-in step Ambry pays after 'Set new password'

apps.name: Notion
apps.what: Email → temporary login code or magic link; a password is optional, so 'forgot password' is rarely reached.

aspects.aspect: Passwordless removes the flow
aspects.why: Same as Slack; Notion's version is the mainstream mobile shape

apps.name: Baymard / uxpatterns.dev (reset pattern)
apps.what: Prefill the address from the sign-in field; tell people what happens next; keep requirements short; validate live.

aspects.aspect: Prefill from the sign-in field
aspects.why: The address was just typed one screen earlier — carrying it over is 20 keystrokes saved

aspects.aspect: Avoid complex password requirements
aspects.why: Ambry's single 8-char floor is right; the suggested-password path keeps it invisible

directions.name: Reset lands you inside
directions.pitch: Carry the address over, stash it with the pending token, and sign in automatically once the new password is set.
regions: Forgot: title, email Input prefilled from sign-in's field (route param), 'Send reset link', 'Back to sign in'
Sent state as today + an 'Open Mail' button (Linking 'message://') beside 'Use a different email'
Reset: title, new-password Input, 'Set new password', Cancel
Success: signInWithPassword(stashed email, new password) → pendingInviteRoute ?? '/' ; if no stash (other device) → today's sign-in notice
Dead token → forgot with 'expired' notice (unchanged)

borrowed.aspect: The link that logs you in

directions.cost: 0 keystrokes if the email was typed on sign-in + 1 tap; link; 1 QuickType tap + 1 tap → inside. Removes the final 2-tap re-sign-in and one screen visit.
directions.tradeoff: Client-only: no server change (Better Auth still issues no session; the client simply signs in with what it holds). Amends spec 28 §UX item 3 (routes to sign-in). The stash is a plain email in AsyncStorage for ≤1 h — same class as the pending invite stash.

directions.name: Sign in with a code instead
directions.pitch: 'Forgot password?' becomes 'Email me a sign-in code'; changing the password moves into Profile → Account.
regions: Sign-in: link 'Email me a sign-in code'
Code screen: 'We sent a code to {email}', one-time-code Input (AutoFill), Continue, Resend, 'Back to sign in'; neutral copy for every address
Profile → Account → 'Change password' SettingsRow → TextPrompt-style sheet (current password not required when signed in on this device; Face ID optional)
Reset-by-link stays as the fallback for old emails

borrowed.aspect: Passcode/possession as proof for a change

directions.cost: Locked-out person: 1 tap + 1 QuickType tap + 1 tap, no password invented. Password change: 2 taps + typing, signed in.
directions.tradeoff: Escalation against docs/adr/auth.md O2 (no second passwordless deep-link path). Needs a Worker OTP route + email template + a change-password route; the biggest win for the locked-out case of the three.

directions.name: Passkey after first sign-in
directions.pitch: Offer Face ID sign-in once inside, so there is nothing to forget next time.
regions: After first sign-in: a one-time card on Profile (or a toast action) 'Sign in with Face ID next time' → enrol
Sign-in screen unchanged; QuickType offers the passkey above the keyboard
Profile → Account → 'Face ID sign-in' SettingsRow (on/off)
Forgot/reset flow unchanged as the fallback
directions.cost: Returning sign-in: 1 tap + Face ID; the forgot flow is reached far less often.
directions.tradeoff: Largest lift: Better Auth passkey plugin, WebAuthn RP on the Worker domain, and a native ASAuthorization module → a new EAS dev build (the §Decisions 5 class of change). Does not fix the locked-out case itself; pairs with either direction above.

current_summary: Onboarding: 'Set up your kitchen' + one-line subtitle; card 'Start a household' (Input prefilled 'Home', chips Home · Our place, 'Create household' live on arrival); card 'Join a household' (Input for code or pasted link, 'Join'); a 44pt 'Sign out'. First run (only after a fresh create): 'You're all set', one step 'Bring your household' (invite lives on Profile), footnote that Pantry/Fridge/Freezer exist, 'Start adding' → /add, 'Look around first' → /. Add household: ScreenHeader + the same two cards without the prefill. Cost today: create = 1 tap (+1 on first-run = 2 to the Add tab); join by pasted link = long-press → Paste → Join → confirm sheet Join = 4 taps; typed code = 16 keystrokes + 1 tap.

apps.name: Bring!
apps.what: Creating a list asks straight away whether to share it; an existing list is shared by long-press → 'Invite Friends' or ⋯ → Settings; the invite goes to the friend's Bring! email and is also shown inside their app on next open; participants are managed from the list's gear.

aspects.aspect: Sharing offered as a yes/no at creation time
aspects.why: Turns 'Bring your household' from an explanation into the thing itself, at the one moment it is relevant

aspects.aspect: The invitation also appears inside the invitee's app
aspects.why: A second delivery channel that survives a lost email

apps.name: AnyList
apps.what: ⋯ → Share, Email & Print → Share List → type an email; existing users get a push and the list appears; new users get an email to download and must register with the same address.

aspects.aspect: Existing users are added with no accept step
aspects.why: Counter-example to spec 43's always-confirm rule — right for an addressed invite, wrong for an anonymous link; keep confirm for links

apps.name: OurGroceries
apps.what: One shared account per household: Settings → 'Share Your Lists' sends an invitation that installs the app if needed and signs the invitee into the same account; alternatively they type the shared email + password.

aspects.aspect: The invitation bootstraps install + sign-in in one step
aspects.why: Ambry's Worker fallback page already does 'get the app'; the missing half is landing the new install on the stashed invite, which spec 43 covers only when the link is tapped after install

apps.name: Apple Family Sharing
apps.what: Settings → [name] → Family → Add Member → Invite People (Messages/Mail) or in person (they enter their Apple Account password on your device); invitee taps the invitation → Join; status and 'resend' per person under Family.

aspects.aspect: Invite in person — the joiner acts on the owner's phone
aspects.why: Two people in one kitchen is the common case; no link needs to travel

aspects.aspect: Per-person invite status with resend
aspects.why: The owner can see who has not joined yet

apps.name: Splitwise
apps.what: Groups tab → 'Start a group' is the primary path; members are added from group settings; a share link lives in group settings; joining happens from the link or by entering a code under 'Join a group'.

aspects.aspect: Create and join are not peers on one screen
aspects.why: Link arrivals never see Ambry's onboarding (they are stashed to the confirm sheet), so the Join card is serving only the typed-code minority

apps.name: Apple HIG — Onboarding
apps.what: Postpone non-essential setup, provide defaults, keep prerequisite flows brief, make tutorials skippable.

aspects.aspect: Defaults over setup
aspects.why: The prefilled 'Home' already follows this; first-run is the remaining prerequisite screen

directions.name: Create is the screen, join is a row
directions.pitch: One primary action and one quiet row; the join card collapses into a TextPrompt.
regions: Title + subtitle
Household name: Input prefilled 'Home' + chips (as today)
Button 'Create household' (primary, live)
SettingsRow 'Have an invite code or link?' (chevron) → TextPrompt with the paste field + Join; a pasted link routes to /join/<token> as today
Error line under the prompt; 'Sign out' text link at the bottom
add-household: same body under a ScreenHeader, no prefill
directions.cost: Create 1 tap (unchanged). Typed code: 1 tap + 16 keystrokes + 1 tap (was 16 + 1). Pasted link: 1 tap + paste (2) + Join = 4 (unchanged).
directions.tradeoff: Join is one tap further away for the typed-code minority; the screen stops presenting two equal cards for one decision most people have already made. Alert.prompt on iOS cannot show a Paste button, so the paste stays the keyboard's own.

directions.name: Share at creation
directions.pitch: First-run becomes the invite: 'Who shares this kitchen?' with one Share button.
regions: 'Home is ready' (largeTitle) + footnote about the three locations
Tile row: household initial + 'Just you so far'
Button 'Invite your household' → creates a spec-43 link (no limit · 7 days) and opens the share sheet
Button (bordered) 'Just me for now' → /add
Toast after sharing: 'Invite link shared · Start adding'

borrowed.aspect: Invite people right after the group exists

directions.cost: Solo person: 1 tap (same as today's 'Start adding'). Couple: 1 tap → share sheet, versus today's read-the-explanation → later find Profile → Share (3+ taps).
directions.tradeoff: Creates a live 7-day link only when tapped (nothing on arrival). Replaces the one message §Decisions 4 kept with the action it described — arguably the same decision, delivered as a control rather than copy.

directions.name: Delete first-run
directions.pitch: Create → straight to Add, with a one-time toast carrying the locations footnote.
regions: Onboarding as today
On create: router.replace('/add') + toast 'Home created · Pantry, Fridge, Freezer are ready'
Profile → Members already shows 'Just you so far — share your invite link'
Optional: one-time Profile tab badge until the first invite is shared

borrowed.aspect: Postpone non-essential setup; no prerequisite screens

directions.cost: −1 tap for everyone (create → Add is 1 tap).
directions.tradeoff: Contradicts critique §Decisions 4 (keep first-run) — escalate in the PR. The invite explanation moves to the place it already lives (Members footnote), which is only found by people who open Profile.

current_summary: LargeTitle 'Profile' over one long inset-grouped scroll: Account (Your name — inline editor; About you bio + links — inline editor; View my public profile), Household (switcher row → sheet with pencil-rename TextPrompt; invite-code row with tap-to-copy, Share, ⋯ Regenerate; Share invite link row → options sheet; Active links list + Revoke all; Leave/Delete household), Behaviour (two dependent switches + footnote), Learned shelf lives (list + Reset), Members (count, per-member ⋯), Notifications (Daily reminder switch, read-only Time), Plan (plan, AI-scans meter, Get/Manage Ambry Plus), About (Privacy Policy, Crash reports), an unheaded exit group (Sign out, Delete account), version, OFF attribution. Cost today: most rows 1 tap; Share invite link 1 tap → sheet → 1 tap; rename 4 taps + typing; the real cost is scrolling ~25 rows across 9 headers to find anything, and two inline save-model editors (name, bio) that S11 still counts.

apps.name: Apple Settings (iOS 18)
apps.what: Account card (photo + name) at the top pushing to the Apple Account screen; then grouped sections in order of use; search; each section has a short header description.

aspects.aspect: Identity card as a header that pushes
aspects.why: Name, bio, links and public profile are one object (the person) and can live one push away instead of as three top-level rows

aspects.aspect: Most-used first, domains not switches at the top level
aspects.why: Profile's top level today mixes identity, a credential, switches, a meter and legal

apps.name: Apple HIG — Settings
apps.what: Keep task-specific options in the screens they affect; minimise the count; defaults over configuration; a custom settings area holds only the rarely changed.

aspects.aspect: Options belong with the task
aspects.why: The two out-lifecycle switches are about the Out/grocery behaviour and could sit on that surface's overflow rather than in a global list

apps.name: Notion — My account
apps.what: Photo, name, email → security (password, 2-step, passkeys) → log out of all devices → delete account near the end; preferences after.

aspects.aspect: Security-adjacent placement of sign-out-everywhere and delete
aspects.why: Ambry has no 'sign out other devices' and no in-app change-password; Notion shows where they belong when they arrive

apps.name: Strava — You tab
apps.what: The tab is the person (activities, stats); settings are behind a gear: units, feed, privacy, notifications, subscription, integrations, credentials.

aspects.aspect: Person page vs settings page
aspects.why: Ambry's Profile is a settings list wearing a profile name; splitting the two is one option

apps.name: Overcast
apps.what: Settings with a 'Nitpicky Details' section holding rarely-changed playback toggles at the bottom.

aspects.aspect: Rarely-touched toggles grouped last under an honest label
aspects.why: Behaviour + Learned shelf lives + Crash reports are Ambry's nitpicky details

apps.name: Instagram — Settings and privacy
apps.what: Accounts Center pinned at the top; long settings list with search.

aspects.aspect: Search over a long settings list
aspects.why: Only worth it past ~40 rows; Ambry is at ~25 — a reason to reorganise rather than add search

directions.name: Account card + household hub
directions.pitch: Two objects on the tab — you, and your kitchen — each one push away.
regions: LargeTitle 'Profile'

GroupedRow identity card: initial tile, name, email, 'Free'/'Ambry Plus' → pushes Account (Your name via TextPrompt, About you, public profile, Plan + meter + CTA, Notifications, Sign out, Delete account)

SectionHeader 'Household' → GroupedRow card 'Home · 3 members' → pushes Household (switcher, rename, Invite people [code copy, Share link, active links], Members, Behaviour, Learned shelf lives, Leave/Delete)
SectionHeader 'About' → Privacy Policy, Crash reports
Version + attribution
directions.cost: Every task +1 tap (invite: 2 → 3 taps; sign out: 2). The tab itself drops from ~25 rows to 4.
directions.tradeoff: P5 just shipped the flat rebuild; re-nesting is a second rebuild and costs a tap on the invite, the most important row. Do only if the flat list proves hard to scan on device.

directions.name: Flat, three groups, invite as one row
directions.pitch: Keep one scroll; regroup You · Your household · Preferences · About; collapse the three invite surfaces into one row.
regions: You: Your name (TextPrompt), About you (pushed editor), Public profile, Plan row + meter + CTA
Your household: switcher row; 'Invite people' row → BottomSheet with the code (tap to copy), Share invite link, active links list, Regenerate in red; Members list; Leave/Delete
Preferences (last, Overcast-style): Daily reminder + Time, the two Behaviour switches + footnote, Learned shelf lives, Crash reports
About: Privacy Policy; exit group; version
directions.cost: Share invite link 1 → 2 taps; every other row unchanged; ~40% shorter scroll; kills the two inline editors (S11's remaining half).
directions.tradeoff: Loses the one-tap share; the code and the links stop being three rows. Keeps P5's IA. Bio/links need a pushed screen (the spec 10 follow-up already says so).

directions.name: Person here, kitchen on the Pantry tab
directions.pitch: Profile is the person; household settings open from the Pantry tab's title.
regions: Profile: identity, public profile, plan, notifications, about, exit — no household rows
Pantry tab: LargeTitle subtitle shows the household name (IA-3) and a header ⋯ OverflowMenu → 'Household settings' (switch, rename, invite, members, behaviour, learned), 'Add location', 'Insights'
Household screen: same rows as today's Household + Members + Behaviour + Learned groups
directions.cost: Invite: Pantry ⋯ → Household → Share = 3 taps (was 2 from Profile). Profile tab drops to ~10 rows.
directions.tradeoff: Two settings homes is a discoverability risk; but it answers IA-3 (nothing outside Profile says which household you are in) by making the household's settings live where the pantry is. Needs the Pantry header overflow P3 did not add.

current_summary: Reached from a Universal Link (or pantry://join fallback). States: spinner 'Checking the invite'; dead link (glyph + neutral sentence + Close); unreachable (cloud glyph + ErrorState with retry + Close); already a member → toast + switch + home; signed out → token stashed, redirect to sign-in with the 'Sign in to join {name}' banner; signed in → a BottomSheet 'Join {name}?' + 'You'll share this household's pantry, grocery list, and expiry reminders' + Join + Cancel, floating over an empty grey screen. Cost today: 1 tap (happy path).

apps.name: Discord
apps.what: Opening an invite shows a splash: server icon and name, online and total member counts, then Accept Invite / No Thanks; some privacy settings can be adjusted before joining.

aspects.aspect: Show what you are joining — name, icon, how many people
aspects.why: A join is a commitment; the sheet today shows a name only

aspects.aspect: Accept / No Thanks as two equal-weight exits
aspects.why: Ambry's Cancel is bare text; a bordered secondary now exists

apps.name: WhatsApp group links
apps.what: Opening a link shows a preview with the group name and member count; the button is Join Group, or Request to Join when admins approve members; a QR sits beside the link; admins can reset the link.

aspects.aspect: Preview with member count before the button
aspects.why: Same argument as Discord, in a household-sized product

aspects.aspect: Request-to-join as the owner-approval mode
aspects.why: Ambry's analogue is the use cap; an approval mode is a possible future spec, not a screen change

apps.name: Apple Family Sharing
apps.what: The invitation arrives in Messages/Mail; tap → Join Family → sign in with the invited Apple Account → confirm what you share; the organiser sees per-person status.

aspects.aspect: Confirm step says what you will share and which account you are
aspects.why: Ambry's body line does the first; a 'Signed in as {email} — not you?' line would do the second, which matters because links are opened on shared devices

apps.name: AnyList
apps.what: Existing users receive a push and the shared list simply appears — no accept step; new users register with the invited email.

aspects.aspect: A push notification carries the invite to a known user
aspects.why: For an addressed invite (not a link) the notification is the landing; Ambry has push already

apps.name: Bring!
apps.what: The emailed invitation is also displayed inside the app on next open.

aspects.aspect: Second in-app delivery of a pending invite
aspects.why: Ambry's stash already does this for the signed-out case; the signed-in case could surface a pending invite on Pantry too

directions.name: A landing, not a sheet on grey
directions.pitch: Full-screen invite card: who, how many, what you share, which account, then Join.
regions: Top: household initial tile (category tint) + 'You're invited to Home'
Line: 'N members' (needs the preview route to return a count — optional; omit if not added)
Body: what you will share (today's sentence)
Row: 'Signed in as {email}' + text link 'Not you? Switch account' (signs out and stashes the token)
Button 'Join' (primary) + Button 'Not now' (bordered)
Error line (FailureNotice) for RPC refusals; dead/unreachable states reuse the same card with the glyph and a bordered Close
directions.cost: 1 tap (unchanged); 'Not you' adds an exit that today costs Cancel → Profile → Sign out → link again.
directions.tradeoff: Member count in the preview leaks household size to anyone holding the link — small, and the owner shared it deliberately; keep it optional. Retires the BottomSheet here (no backdrop-dismiss ambiguity).

directions.name: Sheet over the destination
directions.pitch: Keep the sheet but raise it over the household it opens into.
regions: Underneath: the Pantry tab rendered dimmed (only when the user already has a household; otherwise fall back to the landing card)
BottomSheet with title 'Join Home?', initial tile, share line, 'Signed in as' line, Join + Cancel (Cancel row required: the sheet's one action commits)
directions.cost: 1 tap.
directions.tradeoff: Router complexity: the join route sits outside (tabs); rendering the tab tree under a modal for a user who may be mid-onboarding is the hard case. Least change to copy and state machine.

directions.name: Addressed invites with a push
directions.pitch: Invite a person by email; if they already have Ambry, a push opens the same confirm.
regions: Profile → Invite people sheet gains 'Invite by email' (TextPrompt)
Joiner: push 'Sam invited you to Home' → /join/<token> landing card
Non-user: the existing email/link fallback page
Owner: per-invite status row (Sent · Joined) with Resend
directions.cost: Joiner: 1 tap on the push + 1 tap Join.
directions.tradeoff: New spec: an email-lookup that must not reveal whether an address has an account (owner always sees 'Invite sent'); a Worker route + Resend template; push only where a device token exists. The always-confirm rule stays.

current_summary: ScreenHeader 'Delete account'; red lead 'This is permanent…'; three cards: What gets deleted (4 bullets), What stays (2), Your subscription (+ 'Manage subscriptions' button); a 'Transfer ownership first' card appears on a 409 with the blocking households and 'Go to Profile'; prompt 'Type DELETE to confirm'; Input; 'Delete my account' armed only once the word is typed AND committed (Done/blur); footnote hint. No Alert (S12). Cost today: 6 keystrokes + Done + 1 tap ≈ 8 interactions; the keyboard opens on an irreversible screen.

apps.name: Notion
apps.what: Settings → your name → 'Delete my account' → a dialog lists which workspaces die with the account → type your account email → button 'Permanently delete account and N workspaces'; 30-day best-effort restore via support.

aspects.aspect: The button label carries the consequence count
aspects.why: Ambry knows which households die (sole member) and how many items they hold; saying '…and 1 household' beats a generic 'Delete my account'

apps.name: Instagram (Accounts Center)
apps.what: Manage accounts → Deactivation or deletion → pick the account → Delete → reason picker → password → 30-day grace during which logging in cancels the deletion.

aspects.aspect: Password/identity as the gate, a reason as a control
aspects.why: The gate is a credential the person already has; no invented word

aspects.aspect: Grace period, cancelled by signing in
aspects.why: Forgiveness (agency principle) for the one action Ambry cannot undo

apps.name: Discord
apps.what: Password (+2FA) to confirm; the account sits 'pending deletion' ~14 days; opening the app in that window offers Restore Account.

aspects.aspect: Pending state with Restore on next sign-in
aspects.why: The safety net is on the sign-in screen, where a regretful person will be

apps.name: Apple Account
apps.what: privacy.apple.com → Request to delete → review what happens → an access code is issued for tracking/cancelling; processing can take days. On a trusted device, security changes are gated by the device passcode.

aspects.aspect: Device passcode / biometrics as proof for a critical change
aspects.why: A Face ID prompt is a keyboard-free gate that is at least as deliberate as typing DELETE

apps.name: Apple — Guideline 5.1.1(v)
apps.what: Deletion must be easy to find, must delete (not merely deactivate) the account and data, and must revoke Sign in with Apple tokens.

aspects.aspect: Grace periods are allowed only if the deletion actually completes
aspects.why: Bounds the Instagram/Discord direction: a pending state must still end in deletion

apps.name: iOS power-off slider
apps.what: Hold side + volume until the slider appears, then drag 'slide to power off' — a drag/hold gesture as the confirmation for a consequential action.

aspects.aspect: A hold or drag as the deliberate act, not a typed word
aspects.why: A press-and-hold with a progress fill costs one gesture and no keyboard

directions.name: Consequence in the button, Face ID as the gate
directions.pitch: The screen says exactly what dies, the button repeats it, and Face ID replaces the typed word.
regions: ScreenHeader
Red lead
Card 'What gets deleted' with counts from the cache: 'Home — 42 items, 3 locations', 'Your 7 recipes', photos
Card 'What stays'
Card 'Your subscription' (as today)
Blocked card on 409 (as today)
Button (destructive fill) 'Delete account and 1 household' → LocalAuthentication prompt → run
Fallback when biometrics are unavailable: today's typed word
directions.cost: 1 tap + Face ID (was ~8 interactions and a keyboard).
directions.tradeoff: expo-local-authentication is a native module → a new EAS dev build (§Decisions 5 class). S12's ladder names 'a typed word' for irreversible-and-total; a biometric gate is stronger and keyboard-free — amend the rule in the PR. Counts must come from the cache (no new route).

directions.name: Hold to delete
directions.pitch: Press and hold the button for two seconds; a fill shows progress; release early cancels.
regions: Same cards as today
A destructive Button with a 2 s hold (reanimated progress fill, haptic at completion), label 'Hold to delete my account'
Footnote 'Press and hold for two seconds' (also the accessibilityHint); VoiceOver users get an accessibilityAction that opens a one-question Alert instead
directions.cost: 1 gesture, no keyboard, no native module.
directions.tradeoff: A custom gesture is less familiar than a typed word or a system prompt (familiarity principle); needs the VoiceOver fallback; Maestro cannot hold-press reliably, so the acceptance flow stops at the disabled/enabled assertion as it does today.

directions.name: Grace period
directions.pitch: Deletion schedules; signing in within 14 days offers Restore.
regions: Same screen and gate as today
After confirm: signed out, toast 'Your account will be deleted on {date}'
Sign-in for a pending account: card 'This account is scheduled for deletion on {date}' + Restore account + Continue deleting
Server: pending flag + a cron that runs today's transactional delete after the window
directions.cost: Unchanged taps; adds a safety net.
directions.tradeoff: Spec 11 puts grace/soft delete explicitly out of scope — escalation. Shared households: the 409 transfer-first check must run at schedule time AND at execution; a pending owner blocks others for two weeks. Allowed by 5.1.1(v) only if deletion still completes.

current_summary: Empty ScreenHeader (back chevron) + LargeTitle 'Ambry Plus' with the usage meter as subtitle; lead sentence ('Everything you do by hand is free, forever…'); benefits card (checkmark rows from the server payload); either a 'You're on Ambry Plus' card + Manage subscriptions, or two radio option rows Monthly / Yearly (yearly preselected, savings badge, trial label only when the Apple Account is eligible), the 3.1.2 renewal disclosure ABOVE the CTA, 'Start free trial'/'Subscribe', 'Restore purchases' (secondary), Terms · Privacy links; a dark build shows the prices and a coming-soon line with no CTA. Cost today: 1 tap + the StoreKit sheet (Face ID). Price: the brief's decided figures are $4.99/mo · $29.99/yr · 14-day trial; specs/monetization.md, docs/adr/monetization.md D2 and STATIC_PACKAGES still say $2.99 · $24.99 · 7 days — the PR that changes the screen must move all three.

apps.name: Apple HIG — In-app purchase
apps.what: Show the total billing price per option; intro price, its duration and the standard price after ('1 month free, then $4.99 per month'); a way to restore; do not upsell existing subscribers; show the store only when payments are possible; use the system confirmation sheet.

aspects.aspect: One sentence: trial, then price
aspects.why: Ambry's disclosure already does this; the design question is what is loudest — the billed price must be

apps.name: App Review 3.1.2 (via RevenueCat's rejection guide)
apps.what: Price, duration and renewal terms plus Terms/Privacy links on the purchase surface; rejections when the free trial is more conspicuous than the billed amount; restore required.

aspects.aspect: Billed price more prominent than the trial
aspects.why: Today the savings badge and 'Start free trial' are louder than '$29.99 per year'

apps.name: Bear Pro
apps.what: $2.99/mo or $29.99/yr with a 7-day trial on both; the subscribe surface is a 'Bear Pro' header inside Settings; concrete feature nouns (sync, encryption, export, themes, OCR); one subscription covers all devices on the Apple ID.

aspects.aspect: The sale lives in Settings as a header card
aspects.why: The Plan group in Profile could be the paywall for the browsing case, leaving the full screen for the quota-exhausted moment

aspects.aspect: Concrete nouns, same price shape as Ambry's decided one
aspects.why: Bear's $29.99/yr is the exact figure decided for Ambry — a familiar anchor

apps.name: Fantastical Premium
apps.what: Individual and Family (up to 5) plans, 14-day trial without a card, feature list (scheduling, calendar sets, conferencing, Watch).

aspects.aspect: Family plan beside individual
aspects.why: A household app selling per-user Plus should at least say how a household is covered (spec 23 §4a left Family Sharing OFF for v1 — the paywall should state the answer either way)

aspects.aspect: 14-day trial
aspects.why: Matches the decided trial length; Fantastical is the precedent for 14 over 7

apps.name: CARROT Weather
apps.what: Three tiers (Premium / Premium Ultra / Premium Family) with a feature comparison and a 7-day trial.

aspects.aspect: Free-vs-paid comparison as the persuasion
aspects.why: Ambry's story is 'everything by hand is free'; a two-column comparison says it in one glance

apps.name: Flighty Pro
apps.what: No free trial; weekly/monthly/annual/lifetime plus family tiers; the free app is usable; one headline benefit.

aspects.aspect: One headline benefit above the plans
aspects.why: 'World's fastest delay alerts' beats a checklist; Ambry's is the receipt camera

apps.name: Lifesum (anti-pattern)
apps.what: Carousel of plan cards; greyed-out locked features and upgrade prompts throughout the free experience.

aspects.aspect: Do not gate with greyed-out features everywhere
aspects.why: Ambry's decided posture is three paywall entrances and no nags

directions.name: One plan, one line
directions.pitch: A single headline, a Monthly | Yearly segment, and one big price line — the billed price is the loudest thing on the screen.
regions: ScreenHeader '' + LargeTitle 'Ambry Plus' (subtitle: usage)
Headline: 'Point the camera at the receipt. Plus files it.'
Three benefit rows (from the payload: scans, ideas, members)
SegmentedControl Monthly | Yearly (Yearly default)
Price line in fontSize.figure: '$29.99 / year' with a caption 'that's $2.50 a month · 2 months free' (badge demoted to caption)
Disclosure sentence: '14-day free trial, then $29.99 per year. Charged when the trial ends…' (or 'Charged now' when ineligible)
Button 'Start free trial' / 'Subscribe'
Button (secondary) 'Restore purchases'; Terms · Privacy
Dark build: same layout, no CTA, coming-soon line (unchanged)
directions.cost: 1 tap + StoreKit sheet (unchanged); one fewer object to read (the radio rows become a segment).
directions.tradeoff: A segment for a purchase choice is Ambry's own idiom (ConfirmSheet's location segment) but hides the other price until toggled — both prices must still be visible at once for 3.1.2, so the caption states the monthly figure too.

directions.name: Comparison card
directions.pitch: Free vs Plus as a two-column table above the plans.
regions: Header as today
GroupedRow table: rows Receipt scans / Recipe ideas / Household members / Recipe photos; columns Free | Plus, values from the payload (limit, plus_limit, ideas_limit, ideas_plus_limit; member cap)
Footnote 'Everything you add by hand stays free.'
Family line: 'One Plus per person; your household's cap follows its owner' (or Family Sharing, if 4a flips)
Plans, disclosure, CTA, Restore, links as today

borrowed.aspect: Say how a family is covered

directions.cost: 1 tap + sheet.
directions.tradeoff: Tables fight Dynamic Type — needs useLargeText stacking (each row becomes 'Free 10 · Plus 300'); adds reading before the price. Strongest for the browsing entrance from Profile.

directions.name: Settings card as the sale
directions.pitch: Profile's Plan group becomes the paywall for browsers; the full screen survives for the quota-exhausted entrance.
regions: Profile → Plan: GroupedRow card with the meter, one benefit line, price line + disclosure sentence, Button 'Start free trial' that calls purchasePlus directly, small 'Restore' + Terms · Privacy links inside the card
Quota-exhausted → /paywall (as today)
Plus subscriber: the card shows 'Ambry Plus · renews {date}' + Manage subscriptions
directions.cost: From Profile: 1 tap + sheet (−1 push).
directions.tradeoff: 3.1.2 wants price, terms and links on the purchase surface, so the card carries a disclosure paragraph and two links inside a grouped list — crowded, and the riskiest for review. Keep only if the card can carry the full disclosure legibly.

current_summary: Pushed from the Pantry tab's 'This month' card. ScreenHeader 'This month'; a figure card ('87%' / 'used up' / '20 eaten · 3 went off') or a spinner or 'Not enough this month to say anything useful yet.'; one observation sentence when a food expired 3+ times; SectionHeader 'What went off' + GroupedRow list (name · date); pull-to-refresh. No actions (I-B1 dead end), a failed query reads as 'not enough' (I-A1), the figure card looks tappable and is not (I-C2). Cost today: 1 tap from Pantry; nothing to do once there.

apps.name: Apple Fitness — Summary
apps.what: Rings first (Move/Exercise/Stand), then sections: workouts, Trends (90 days vs 365, arrows), awards; tap the rings for history; metrics are customisable.

aspects.aspect: A trend arrow instead of a chart
aspects.why: 'vs your usual' is one glyph and one number — no time-series screen, which spec 39 forbids

apps.name: Oura — Readiness
apps.what: A 0–100 score with a label band (Optimal / Good / Fair / Pay attention), a crown at 85+, a list of contributors with bars, one recommendation sentence, tap a contributor for detail.

aspects.aspect: Score → contributors → one sentence
aspects.why: Ambry already has the three parts; the label band and per-contributor detail are the missing shape

aspects.aspect: Contributors are tappable for the why
aspects.why: 'Salad leaves went off 3 times' should open the three rows and the fix

apps.name: YNAB — Spending Breakdown
apps.what: Categories by percentage under the chart; filters for date, categories, accounts; tap a category to see its transactions; on mobile since 2024.

aspects.aspect: Group by category with a count, one tap to the rows
aspects.why: Ambry's list is per row; grouping 'Dairy ×4' makes the pattern visible without a chart

apps.name: Copilot Money — Month in Review
apps.what: Appears in the Transactions tab at the turn of the month as a set of slides (spending, income, investments, trends); any slide can be shared.

aspects.aspect: A month-end moment rather than a permanent screen
aspects.why: Gives the scorecard a reason to be opened on the 1st, when the month is complete

apps.name: Too Good To Go
apps.what: Impact framed per action ('every Surprise Bag equates to 2.7kg of CO2e avoided').

aspects.aspect: Per-item equivalence
aspects.why: Tempting for 'eaten' rows; but spec 39 bans invented numbers (no money) and a kg-CO2e figure per food would be one — record as rejected

apps.name: NoWaste
apps.what: A 'My numbers' widget on the profile shows personal food-waste stats.

aspects.aspect: Stats on the profile
aspects.why: Ambry chose the Pantry tab (spec 39); keep it — the profile is the account, not the kitchen

directions.name: Contributors and one fix
directions.pitch: Group what went off by food, and let each group carry the action the observation implies.
regions: ScreenHeader 'This month'
Figure (not pressable) with a label band under the %: 'Tight ship' ≥90 · 'Good' 75–89 · 'Worth a look' <75
Observation sentence
SectionHeader 'What went off'

GroupedRow per food: 'Salad leaves' · '×3' · trailing SwipeRow actions 'Remind sooner' (shortens the household's learned shelf life via spec 40's override) and 'Add to list'; tap expands the dated rows
ErrorState with retry on a failed query; the 'not enough' line only when the query succeeded
Pull-to-refresh as today

borrowed.aspect: Group with counts, tap to rows

directions.cost: 1 tap to open (unchanged); 1 swipe + tap to act on a repeat offender (was: navigate to Profile → Learned shelf lives).
directions.tradeoff: Closes I-B1, I-A1 and I-C2 in one package. The 'Remind sooner' write needs a spec 39/40 amendment naming which value changes; label-band copy must obey 'never scold' (jest-pinned strings).

directions.name: Versus your usual
directions.pitch: One extra line under the figure: this month against last month, with an arrow.
regions: Figure as today
Line: '▲ 5 points vs August' or '— about the same' (needs one more month in the outcomes query, no schema change)
Everything else as today
directions.cost: 0 extra interactions.
directions.tradeoff: Spec 39 says 'monthly, not lifetime' and puts multi-month trends out of scope; a single prior-month comparison is a small contradiction — escalate. Cheapest of the three.

directions.name: Month-end moment
directions.pitch: On the 1st, the finished month arrives as a card (and an optional push) with a shareable line.
regions: Pantry tab, first week of the month: 'August: 87% used up' card above 'This month' (dismissable)
Push at digest time on the 1st: 'August: 87% used up · 3 went off' → /insights?month=2026-08
Insights: month picker (This month | Last month segment), a Share button (text only: the counts line) in ScreenHeader's right slot
Rest of the screen as today
directions.cost: 1 tap from the push.
directions.tradeoff: Push needs spec 16's scheduler; an image share would need a view-shot native module (new build) so share text only. Keeps one month at a time (a Last-month view is still one month), but the segment is a second header control on a small screen.
